artifacts.description: Routed wire paths, harness bundles, ties and clearances (contract)
Routing internals: nodes, bundle segments, bends, mates, holes
Harness BOM: wire cut lengths per AWG/colour, connectors, ties
Cable slack simulation: per-wire minimum clearance to moving parts

assumptions.statement: Catalog convention: box frames sit on their bottom face; x/y-axis cylinders are centred on the component origin; z-axis cylinders (standoffs) start at their mounting face.

Swept volumes sample joint travel at 1 deg (steering about the kingpin); spinning cylinders about their own axis are invariant. Moving parts without joints (motor can, gearbox) use their own envelope.

Voxel A* (3 mm) with length, surface-following, moving-proximity and bend costs, then any-angle string pulling and elastic-rod relaxation; wires of one harness bundle on shared voxels. Harnesses do not avoid each other.
Minimum bend radius = catalog factor x bundle OD, bundle OD from optimal circle packing of the conductors (conservative for loose, untaped wires).
Floating (harness-to-harness) mated pairs are placed at the copper-mass-weighted geodesic optimum with a tie-ability term; mated pair length = sum of bodies - 50% engagement.
Cut length = routed length + route.slack + termination allowances (estimates per connector family: solder cup 5-6 mm, crimp 3 mm, splice 6 mm).
Slack reach uses the ellipsoid |x - p1| + |x - p2| <= L between consecutive pins, ignoring gravity and stiffness (conservative); route slack is distributed uniformly over spans.
Clearance and intersection ignore a termination zone at each end against the component the wire terminates on (and the parts it is mounted on).

XPBD rods, 7.5 mm segments, 0.5 ms substeps; EI from catalog estimates, axial stiffness 0.6 x E_Cu x A; velocity damping 19 1/s (~5 % of critical at 30 Hz) and friction 0.5 are estimates. Wires are simulated individually (no wire-wire contact); moving parts do not push cables, contacts are reported.
